specimen:
Remember me when I am gone away,
Gone far away into the silent land;
When you can no more hold me by the hand,
Nor I half turn to go, yet turning stay.
hook: The word 'away' shows up twice in her first two lines.
tell: Line one ends on 'gone away' and line two opens by repeating it: 'Gone far away.' A model trained to avoid redundancy almost always swaps the repeat for a synonym — 'gone far off,' 'gone from sight' — because near-immediate word repetition reads as a mistake to it. Rossetti repeats the word on purpose, using the echo to make the parting feel incantatory rather than accidental.
title: One word, twice, two lines — that's the human giveaway
caption: A model would swap the second 'away' for a synonym. Rossetti repeats it on purpose — did you catch it before the reveal?
